atoms.b: For the ancient Egyptians, food was never a problem. This is because the Egyptians were successful ((++farmers fathers)).
The rich ((++soil meat)) around the Nile helped them to grow the ((++plants buildings)) they needed.
Most years, there was so much food that it could be ((++traded wasted)) with other countries or stored for years of ((++famine fortune)).

instruction.text: Select the named crop that the Egyptians grew.
Match the ingredients to their use.

b.sound: ground into flour to make bread
made into a hearty and cheap soup
used to flavour dishes and for medicines

instruction.text: The Egyptians also ate meat. Select the correct animal.

feedback.correct: The Egyptians hunted the geese that fed on the plants growing on the banks of the Nile.
The Nile was full of fish. When it flooded, fish would get trapped in shallow pools, making them even easier to catch.
Goats were farmed for their meat. People also raised sheep, pigs and ducks.
